# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[6] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🖐 🤚]

I need to establish communication. I can see the bomb and I can gesture to Mute (and speak to both Mute and Blind, but Blind can't see gestures or read - Blind can only hear speech and feel the bomb). Let me check: Deaf speaks -> Mute and Blind receive (as speech, they can hear... wait, Blind cannot hear either? Let me recheck: Blind "cannot see a colour, gesture, or anything printed" but CAN hear. Mute cannot speak or touch, Deaf cannot hear or touch.

So Deaf speaking reaches Mute and Blind (both can hear). Deaf gesturing reaches only Mute (who can see). Blind gestured to me but I can't receive meaning from gestures they made blind... wait Blind cannot see, but can they gesture? The rules say Blind cannot see gestures, but sending one is a physical act - actually gesture requires seeing to interpret, but Blind could still make gestures without knowing what they mean visually. Regardless, I received blank-like gesture symbols from Blind and Mute - but I CAN see gestures since I'm Deaf (deaf can see). So I received actual symbols.

Mute gestured 👍✌👌 to me - I can see this since I'm Deaf. Blind gestured ✋🖐🤚 to me too - I can see this.

This is turn 1, first round. I should report what I see on the bomb to Mute and Blind via speech, since both can hear me.

```
speak(text="I see: DISPLAY shows 9. LIGHT is blue. STRIP has three sections painted red, green, green in that order. KEYPAD is engraved with digit 1 shows 1, digit 2 shows 5, digit 3 shows 2, digit 4 shows 6, it accepts 1 digit entry, currently nothing entered. WIRES are numbered 1 through 6: white, purple, blue, red, orange, green. Mute, please tell me what the manual says we need to do.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[6] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👋 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👋 ☝ ☝ ☝]

I need to interpret Mute's gesture. Mute can't speak, only gesture to me (Deaf) or... wait, Mute can only gesture, and gestures reach whoever can see - that's me (Deaf). Blind cannot see gestures at all. So Mute is trying to communicate to me using gestures, likely encoding letters or numbers using ☝ (pointing up, maybe "count") separated by 👋 (wave, maybe separator).

Let me count: ☝×6, 👋, ☝×5, 👋, ☝×3

That could be encoding numbers: 6, 5, 3 separated by waves. Or it could be spelling something using tally marks grouped by waves representing letters (A=1, F=6, etc.) - 6=F, 5=E, 3=C? "FEC"? Or maybe it's referencing wire numbers or keypad digits.

Given the keypad shows digits 1,5,2,6 and needs 1 digit entered - maybe Mute is telling me which wire/keypad value matters. Groups of 6,5,3 - could reference wire positions (6=green, 5=orange, 3=blue) or could be a countdown/sequence for keypad.

I should acknowledge receipt and ask for clarification, and continue relaying bomb state since DISPLAY changed 9->8 (countdown!). This is urgent - decreasing display suggests a timer.

```
speak(text="Display dropped from 9 to 8, this looks like a countdown timer. Mute, I received three groups of tally-like gestures: six, five, three, separated by waves. Please confirm if these are numbers 6, 5, 3 or something else, and tell me what to do with the keypad or wires. Blind, stand by, do not touch anything yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[6] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👋 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👋 ☝ ☝ ☝]

The display hit 0 and the light changed from blue to yellow - something triggered! This is critical. Mute added a 👍 (thumbs up = confirm) before the same sequence, confirming my interpretation: 6, 5, 3.

The keypad has positions 1:[1], 2:[5], 3:[2], 4:[6] and needs 1 digit entered. The numbers 6,5,3 don't directly map to keypad positions (only 1-4 exist). But wire 6 is green, wire 5 is orange, wire 3 is blue. Or keypad values: position with value 5 is position 2, value 6 is position 4... 3 isn't a value shown except position 3 has value 2.

Given urgency (display at 0, light changed), I need to relay this immediately and let Blind know what to press/cut. Since keypad needs 1 digit typed in, and values are 1,5,2,6 at positions 1-4 - if the code is asking for digit "6" then press position 4 (value 6). But the sequence 6,5,3 might mean cut wires 6, 5, 3 in order, or it could mean something else entirely from the manual.

I must speak urgently to both, since Blind can only hear.

```
speak(text="Urgent: DISPLAY hit 0 and LIGHT changed from blue to yellow, something just triggered. Mute confirmed the sequence is six five three. Blind, do not act yet. Mute, please confirm: is six five three a wire cutting order, or a code for the keypad, or something else? I need to know exactly what action to take before anyone touches anything.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[6] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫲 🫲 🫲 👋 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👋 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👋 ☝ ☝ ☝]

The display is now counting up (0→3), light is yellow. Mute sent a new gesture with 🫲 (left hand grab/pull, possibly meaning "wire" or "cut") repeated 3 times, then the same 6,5,3 sequence.

This strongly suggests: 🫲🫲🫲 = "cut" or "wire" (maybe indicating an action, repeated 3 times could mean "cut 3 wires" or could be a distinct symbol meaning something like "wire" spelled/gestured 3 times as emphasis), followed by the numbers 6, 5, 3.

Most likely interpretation: cut wires 6, 5, 3 in that order. Wire 6 is green, wire 5 is orange, wire 3 is blue.

Given the countdown reset and is climbing again (could be re-arming or a new phase), time is critical. I should relay this as an actionable instruction to Blind now, since Blind can hear my speech.

```
speak(text="Mute's gesture now shows a cutting motion three times followed by six five three. I believe this means cut wires in order: wire six, then wire five, then wire three. Blind, wire six is green, wire five is orange, wire three is blue, but go by the numbers not colors since you cannot see color. Mute, if this is wrong, signal me immediately. Blind, wait for Mute's explicit confirmation before cutting, we have display now climbing from zero, count is at three.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [red] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[6] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

Light is now red — this is escalating fast, display climbing 3→7. Mute sent double thumbs-up, confirming my interpretation: cut wire 6, then 5, then 3, in that order. This is a strong confirmation.

I need to relay this clear, final instruction to Blind immediately since time is critical and the light going red suggests danger is increasing.

```
speak(text="Confirmed twice by Mute with thumbs up. Blind, act now: cut wire six first, then wire five, then wire three, in that exact order. Light just turned red and display is climbing, this is urgent.")
wait()
```
